announcements.title: Headteacher's Message: Welcome to this week’s school newsletter!
announcements.content:
Welcome to this week’s school
newsletter!

As we come to the end of another
busy and successful week at school, it
has been wonderful to see our
children taking part in such a wide
range of activities and events. From
library visits and sporting
competitions to special opportunities
for learning beyond the classroom,
there has been plenty to keep
everyone engaged and inspired.

This week, we have also spent time
reflecting on the importance of
Remembrance Day. On Wednesday at
11:00am, the whole school took part
in a two-minute silence. We were
incredibly proud of all our children,
who showed great respect and
maturity throughout this important
moment of reflection. Our support for
the Poppy Appeal has been fantastic
once again this year. Thanks to the
generosity of our school community,
we have raised a significant amount
through the sale of poppies and other
remembrance merchandise, helping
to support the invaluable work of the
Royal British Legion.

Today, we have also enjoyed
celebrating Children in Need, with
pupils getting involved in fundraising
activities while learning about the
difference their contributions can
make to children and families across
the UK. The children rounded off the
week with a fun-filled and exciting
Children in Need assembly, where
they had the opportunity to challenge
members of staff in a series of head-
to-head competitions, including Bang
Bang Maths, bottle flipping and
balloon keepy-uppies! There was
great excitement throughout the hall,
especially when the children won a
challenge and earned the chance to
see Mrs Flisher get pied.

It was a fantastic way to end the
week, with plenty of laughter and
smiles from both pupils and staff
alike. Thank you to everyone who has
supported our fundraising efforts. We
are also excited to announce that the
winner of our Pudsey Bear raffle will
be drawn on Monday, so keep an eye
out for the result! Thank you, as
always, for your continued support.
We hope you enjoy reading about
some of the highlights from another
memorable week at Warboys Primary
Academy.

announcements.title: School Reminders: Inhalers, Absences & School Dinners
announcements.content:
Important News

and Reminders

Christmas Decoration Sessions 🎄

We are excited to welcome parents
and carers into school for our
Christmas Decoration Sessions,
taking place during the week
commencing

23 November 2026

.
These special afternoons give
children the opportunity to spend
time getting creative with their
families while helping to decorate
their classrooms for the festive
season.

Details of your child's session, along
with year group-specific sign-up
links, can be found in the letter sent
home. Please complete the form as
soon as possible to help us plan
resources and materials.

These are always much-loved events,
and we look forward to sharing some
festive fun and creating wonderful
memories together in the lead-up to
Christmas. ✨

Christmas Food Bank Appeal

As a school community, we are proud
to support some of our vulnerable
families by providing food parcels in
the lead up to Christmas. This
support can make a real difference
during what can be a particularly
challenging time of year for some
households. To help us continue this
important work, we kindly ask
families to donate any non-perishable
food items, toiletries, or festive treats
they may be able to spare. Every
donation, no matter how small, will
help us create Christmas food parcels
for families in need within our school
community. We would like to thank
you in advance for your generosity
and support.

Dunelm Delivering Joy Campaign

We are excited to share that this year
our school will be taking part in the
‘Dunelm Delivering Joy Campaign’,
helping to spread some festive cheer
to children and families in our local
community. Every Christmas,
Dunelm do a collection of gift bags
with presents in for those who are
less fortunate and who may otherwise
receive nothing. Below are the tags
we have chosen and items that would
be great to include in the gift bags.

Homeless man/woman - Thermal hat,
gloves and scarf; thermal flask; throw
blanket; sweet treats.

Families in need – Towels; hot water
bottles; blankets; sweet treats.

If you wish to contribute to any gift
bag donations, please send them in
with your child to pass to their class
teacher, give them to the office, or
give them directly to Miss Le Moel or
Mrs Flisher. Please ensure that any
items are brought into school by
Thursday 3rd December.

Thank you for your support with this
and we look forward to seeing the gift
bags finished!

Parent Consultation
Appointments

We are pleased to let parents and
carers know that

Parent Consultation
appointments are now live and
available to book

.

These meetings provide a valuable
opportunity to discuss your child's
progress, celebrate their
achievements, and talk through any
areas where they may need
additional support. We strongly
encourage all families to book an
appointment with their child's class
teacher.

Appointments can be booked via

MCAS (My Child at School)

. Please
log in to the app and select your
preferred time slot as soon as
possible, as appointments are
allocated on a first-come, first-served
basis.

If you experience any difficulties
booking your appointment, please
contact the school office for
assistance.

Year 4 Residential Visit to
Grafham Water

We are pleased to let Year 4 parents
and carers know that

deposits are
now payable via the MCAS app

for
our exciting residential visit to

Grafham Water

, taking place from

Monday 28th June to Wednesday 30th
June 2027.

To

secure your child’s place, a non-
refundable deposit of £75

is required.
Once the deposit has been paid, the

remaining balance can be paid in
monthly instalments through MCAS.

We hope that offering the opportunity
to spread the cost over an extended
period will help make

budgeting for
the visit a little easier for families.

We are very much looking forward to
what promises to be a

fantastic and
memorable experience for our Year 4
children!

Reminder: School Gates at Drop-
Off and Collection

A polite reminder to all parents and
carers that the

Visitor Gate at the
front of the school is for visitors and
late arrivals only

For the safety of our children and to
help ensure arrival and collection
times run smoothly,

all parents and
carers dropping off or collecting
children should use the designated
side gates.

We kindly ask that you

do not use the
Visitor Gate as an entrance or exit
during normal drop-off and collection
times.

We would also like to remind
everyone that the Visitor Gate

must
NOT be wedged open under any
circumstances

. This gate is
required to remain closed and secure
between visitors to help safeguard
our pupils and maintain the security
of the school site.

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation in helping us keep
our school environment

safe, secure,
and well organised for everyone.

YDP Wraparound Provision:
Booking Reminder

A reminder to parents and carers
wishing to book their child into the

wraparound provision provided by
YDP

that all bookings must be made
directly through the YDP booking
platform, which can be found

HERE

.
Please note that

YDP is a separate
provider

, and therefore the school
office is

unable to make or manage
bookings on behalf of families

Places are limited, so we strongly
encourage families to book as far in
advance as possible to avoid
disappointment.

If you need to make
a

same-day booking

, this must be
completed through the YDP booking
platform

by 1.00pm at the latest

. We
are also pleased to share that YDP
has informed us that they will be
taking on an

additional member of
staff on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and
Thursdays

, which will increase
capacity and allow

more spaces to
become available on these days

Thank you for your cooperation and
for ensuring all bookings are made
directly with YDP.

Uniform Donations

We are very grateful for all the
uniform donations we receive.
However,

we kindly ask that parents
and carers do not bring any more
uniform donations into school at this
time,

as we currently have plenty of
stock. The only items we are still able
to accept are

clean, good-condition
uniform with the school logo

,
specifically:

Jumpers and cardigans

PE tops

Hoodies

Thank you for your understanding
and continued support.

announcements.title: EEBSA-Environmental and Emotional Barriers to Scho
announcements.content:
EEBSA

-Environmental

and Emotional

Barriers to

School

Attendance

Environmental and Emotional
Barriers to School Attendance
(EEBSA) is a term used to describe a
child's difficulty attending or
engaging with school due to
emotional factors. Children may
display EEBSA in a variety of ways,
and recognising the early signs can
help ensure they receive the right
support (please see the image
provided by Cambridgeshire County
Council highlighting signs of
EEBSA).

If you have concerns that your child
may be showing signs of EEBSA,
please speak to your child's class
teacher or a member of the Senior
Leadership Team. By working
together, we can develop a shared
understanding of your child's
strengths and any barriers they may
be facing, with the aim of supporting
their wellbeing and helping them feel
happy and successful at school.

Miss Westwood

will be hosting an
informal

Coffee Afternoon on
Wednesday 18th November from
2:30pm to 3:00pm

. Parents and carers
are warmly invited to attend to find
out more about EEBSA, discuss any
concerns, and learn about the support
available.

We look forward to seeing you there.

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update

We are delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation.

announcements.title: Young Carers: Support & Parent Concern Form
announcements.content:
At our school, we are proud to
support our Young Carers and
recognise the important role they
play within their families. We work
closely with Centre 33 to provide
external support, while internally we
offer fortnightly Young Carers
sessions where children can come
together to chat, share experiences,
take part in activities, and relax in a
supportive environment. Led by Miss
Coles and Mrs Flisher, with support
from Mr Bostock, these sessions help
ensure our Young Carers feel valued,
understood, and supported. We are
also committed to raising awareness
across the school community and
celebrating the dedication, resilience,
and compassion shown by our Young
Carers every day.

Please follow the link below to flag
any child that you may deem to be a
Young Carer. A Young Carer is a
child young person who helps to look
after a family member who may have
an illness, disability, mental health
difficulty, or who may need extra
support for another reason. This care
can include practical tasks, emotional
support, or helping siblings, and it
may take place before or after the
school day. We recognise that these
responsibilities can sometimes impact
a child’s wellbeing, learning, and
emotional needs. All conversations
and responses will be treated
sensitively and in confidence.

announcements.title: Parent Forum
announcements.content:
The Parent Forum provides an
opportunity for parents and carers to
meet with school leaders, share ideas,
ask questions, and discuss topics that
are important to our school
community. It is a friendly and
informal way to strengthen the
partnership between home and
school, ensuring that parent voices
help shape and support the ongoing
development of our school.

For those who are new to our school,
more information about the Parent
Forum, including its purpose and how
it operates, can be found on the

Parent Forum section of our school
website

HERE

.

If there are any topics you would like
to see discussed, please email your
suggestions to

parentforum@wpa.education

We look forward to hearing your
thoughts and ideas. Together, we can
continue to make our school the very
best it can be for all our children.
